guide.summary: Harvest time tracking, public integration (self-serve, wait none); Greenhouse 'Harvest' API, partner OAuth (partner acceptance, wait monthly review cycle plus about 7 business days; plan in months).
guide.verdict: Easiest: Harvest time tracking, public integration (self-serve, wait none). Hardest: Greenhouse 'Harvest' API, partner OAuth (partner acceptance, wait monthly review cycle plus about 7 business days; plan in months).

composio.note: Composio manages OAuth for Harvest, so prototypes need no app of your own.

need_own_app.answer: Not for a prototype, because Composio supplies a managed Harvest app. For launch, use your own app if you want your brand on the consent screen, your own quota, or scopes the managed app lacks.
reasons: Managed app consent screen says Composio wants access, not your app name

prerequisites.title: Confirm which Harvest you mean
prerequisites.detail: Harvest (getharvest.com, Harvest ID) and Greenhouse's Harvest API are different products with different approval paths. The dossier mixes both.

prerequisites.title: Harvest administrator access
prerequisites.detail: The docs say the person registering an app must be logged in as an Administrator on the Harvest account. This comes from the older V1 and GitHub pages.

prerequisites.title: Mutual customer, website and privacy policy
prerequisites.detail: Greenhouse requires at least one mutual customer and an active website with a privacy policy before it considers an application.

steps.title: Draft app settings and scope choice
steps.detail: Prepare the app name, redirect URL and the minimal Products choice (Harvest, Forecast or both), and decide if it is multi-account.
steps.done_when: Settings sheet is ready to paste into the form

steps.title: Create the OAuth2 app in Harvest ID
steps.detail: Log in and create the app in the Developers section of Harvest ID. Paste in the Composio redirect URL.
steps.done_when: You have a client ID and client secret

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your own client ID and secret. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard into the Harvest app.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists for the harvest toolkit

steps.title: Connect a test account and check refresh
steps.detail: Authorize a Harvest account and confirm a call works. Check that token refresh works, since access tokens expire.
steps.done_when: A connected account returns data after a refresh

steps.title: Submit the Greenhouse integration request form
steps.detail: Start the agreement process. This needs business and legal details, and a mutual customer.

steps.title: Wait for monthly review and agreement
steps.detail: Greenhouse reviews on the first Monday of each month and then sends an API agreement. An out-of-cycle review can be requested for an urgent named customer.

steps.title: Request credentials with all redirect URIs
steps.detail: Email partner support with the integration name, 128x128 logo, scopes, environment and every callback URI. Later changes need another email.

traps.title: Each user's access token expires in 18 hours; the
traps.detail: Each user's access token expires in 18 hours; the page does not tie this to testing mode.

traps.title: Two different products named Harvest
traps.detail: Evidence for Greenhouse's Harvest API does not apply to Harvest time tracking, and the reverse. Check which one your users have.

traps.title: Managed app hides your brand and shares quota
traps.detail: With the Composio managed app, users see Composio on the consent screen and quota is shared with all Composio users.

traps.title: Idle partner connections die
traps.detail: The refresh token lasts 14 days and rotates on every refresh, so an idle connection dies at day 15. Adding a scope forces every customer to re-authorize.

traps.title: Redirect URI changes cost an email
traps.detail: You cannot add or edit callback hosts yourself, and each change needs another email to partner support.

blockers.symptom: Greenhouse says your application is not accepted
blockers.what_it_means: Not every partner application is accepted.
blockers.what_to_do: Use the shortcut: have the customer create their own Harvest v3 credentials, or request an out-of-cycle review with a named mutual customer.
blockers.agent_can_help: Draft the request email and the customer setup instructions.

open_questions: Does Harvest (getharvest.com) review or restrict public OAuth apps in practice? Ask Harvest support or test with an outside account.
What do Greenhouse partner reviews check? Ask partner-support@greenhouse.io; the docs do not say.
Is the Greenhouse partner path relevant at all? Confirm which Harvest product your users have.
Is there a fee or plan requirement for Harvest API access? Not found; check Harvest pricing or ask support.
Not found: what each review or verification checks and what the developer must submit. Checked getharvest.com, github.com.
